newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: 5 African states join forces to fight diseases.
newsitem.headline: 5 African states join forces to fight diseases.

text.p: The five states of Africa's Great Lakes region, Burundi, the Congo, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda and Tanzania, signed a pact on Friday vowing to co-operate to halt epidemics such as cholera and malaria.

The World Health Organisation (WHO), in a statement issued at its Geneva headquarters, said the countries would pool stocks of drugs and vaccines, conduct joint research and meet regularly on public health issues.
The document was signed on the last day of a two-day meeting in Kigali, Rwanda, attended by health ministers and officials, according to the United Nations health agency.

Nearly 10 per cent of the population of the five countries are refugees or internally displaced people, creating conditions ripe for the spread of diseases linked to overcrowding such as cholera, typhus, dysentery and malaria.

"Major public health threats which will be top priorities for collaboration include epidemic prevention and the control of infectious diseases with high epidemic potential, such as cholera, epidemic meningitis, bacillary dysentery, measles, viral haemorrhagic fevers, epidemic typhus, epidemic malaria, plague, poliomyelitis and HIV/AIDS," WHO said.
Standardisation of treatment of some diseases such as tuberculosis will permit refugees and other returnee populations to continue treatment in spite of their migrating, it added.
